executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

6 7 ## Key Features 8 9 ### Syntax highlighting 10 11 `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. 12 13 ### Git integration 14 15 `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. 16 17 ### Show non-printable characters 18 19 You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. 20 21 ### Automatic paging 22 23 By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. 24 If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. 25 If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. 26 27 #### File concatenation 28 29 Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. 30 Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. 31 32 ## How to use 33 34 Display a single file on the terminal: 35 36 ```bash 37 bat README.md 38 ``` 39 40 Display multiple files at once: 41 42 ```bash 43 bat src/*.rs 44 ``` 45 46 Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: 47 48 ```bash 49 curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat 50 ``` 51 52 Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: 53 54 ```bash 55 yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json 56 ``` 57 58 Show and highlight non-printable characters: 59 60 ```bash 61 bat -A /etc/hosts 62 ``` 63 64 Use it as a `cat` replacement: 65 66 ```bash 67 bat > note.md # quickly create a new file 68 69 bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md 70 71 bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) 72 73 bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. 74 ``` 75 76 ### Integration with other tools 77 78 #### `fzf` 79 80 You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: 81 82 ```bash 83 fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" 84 ``` 85 86 #### `find` or `fd` 87 88 Preview all search results with `bat`: 89 90 ```bash 91 find … -exec bat {} + 92 fd … -X bat 93 ``` 94 95 #### `ripgrep` 96 97 With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: 98 99 ```bash 100 batgrep needle src/ 101 ``` 102 103 #### `tail -f` 104 105 `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: 106 107 ```bash 108 tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log 109 ``` 110 111 #### `git` 112 113 Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: 114 115 ```bash 116 git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs 117 ``` 118 119 #### `git diff` 120 121 Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: 122 123 ```bash 124 batdiff() { 125 git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff 126 } 127 ``` 128 129 #### `xclip` 130 131 Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: 132 133 ```bash 134 bat main.cpp | xclip 135 ``` 136 137 `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. 138 139 #### `man` 140 141 `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: 142 143 ```bash 144 export MANPAGER="bat -plman" 145 man 2 select 146 ``` 147 148 #### Highlighting `--help` messages 149 150 You can use `bat` to colorize help text: 151 152 ```bash 153 cp --help | bat -plhelp 154 ``` 155 156 Or use a wrapper: 157 158 ```bash 159 alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' 160 help() { 161 "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp 162 } 163 ``` 164 165 ## Installation 166 167 Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. 168 169 `bat` is also available through various package managers: 170 171 -
